newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle quiet, no trade - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle quiet, no trade - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Monday were at a standstill, with bids and offers $2.00 apart, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids $62.00 to $63.00 were passed by owners pricing cattle at $64.00 to $65.00 per cwt.
Sales were not considered likely until Tuesday or Wednesday following last week's active trade, which set a weekly high record in Kansas and left packers with comfortable inventory levels, they said.
Last sales were Friday at $63.00, down $1.00 from Wednesday and down $2.00 to $3.00 from the previous week.

Fed cattle prices last week were pressured by increased supplies of market-ready cattle and a determination to remain current amid outlooks for ever-expanding supplies through the next six weeks, several feedlot sources said.
"There's a lot of cattle in the system right now," one Kansas feedlot manager said.
Showlists this week were seen unchanged, compared with last week, they said.
